subject: GA go/no-go prep: Hosted canary rollouts (Console workflow)
related_links: GitHub: redwood/pr-28895 (fix rollout step stuck on metric timeout)
GitHub: redwood/pr-28877 (rollout activity log + audit events)
Jira: SUP-48377 (canary traffic split not matching config)
body:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 18, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: GA go/no-go prep: Hosted canary rollouts (Console workflow)

Marissa / Naomi,

Putting a leadership-ready snapshot together for the GA go/no-go this week. Can you sanity check the risk callouts + confirm any remaining blockers from Product/Sec?

Current status (engineering):
- Console wizard + backend contracts: ready in staging, dogfooded by 3 internal routes.
- Data plane split enforcement: stable after the us-east split-mismatch follow-up; cohorting looks deterministic across retries/streaming.
- Auto-stop/rollback: wired and tested in staging with injected 5xx + latency regressions.
- Activity timeline: events emitted + visible in Console.

Open items / risks to highlight:
1) Split mismatch regression risk (beta incident)
   - What happened: observed split drifting from configured % in us-east during a capacity event.
   - Mitigation: guardrails on router sampling + better visibility in routing logs; added smoke test coverage.
   - Status: fixed + validated in staging; monitoring plan in place.

2) Rollout step stuck on metric evaluation timeout
   - What happened: orchestrator could stall waiting on cohort metrics query.
   - Mitigation: retries + hard timeout → explicit “metrics unavailable” state (pauses rollout, requires operator action).
   - Status: fix is merged; needs one more soak in canary-prod env.

3) Audit log completeness / governance defaults
   - We believe we cover: create/start/pause/resume/step-change/approve/rollback + auto-stop trigger.
   - Need Sec to confirm: event fields + retention messaging is acceptable for GA.

Proposed GA rollout plan:
- Feature flag: per-tenant enablement; start with 5–10 beta design partners already engaged.
- Week 1: enable in 1 region (us-west) by default; other regions opt-in.
- Week 2: expand to us-east + eu-west once dashboards/alerts are quiet.
- Kill switch: disable canary routing primitive at control plane (routes revert to baseline).

Owners (for leadership slide):
- Eng go/no-go: Dylan (me)
- Product go/no-go: Marissa
- Security/audit go/no-go: Naomi

Requests:
- Marissa: any GA scope deltas vs PM-1859 we should reflect (e.g., default soak, approval gates)?
- Naomi: any remaining audit log schema/retention concerns that would block GA?

Thanks,
Dylan

—
Dylan Brooks
Engineering Lead, Console & Tooling
Redwood Inference



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 18, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: GA go/no-go prep: Hosted canary rollouts (Console workflow)

Dylan — looks good.

Two things I’d add for leadership context:
- “Default guardrails” decision: we’re GA’ing with max step size + min soak time defaults ON, but allowing org admins to tighten (not loosen) without support. Any loosening requires an explicit “advanced” toggle + warning copy.
- Beta learnings: the only customer-facing pain so far was the unexpected auto-pause after a latency spike (support ticket). We should call out that it’s expected behavior + we have tuning guidance.

Can you include:
- Link/mention to the support ticket(s) that informed the tuning guidance.
- A sentence on what “rollback” actually does for Hosted routes (i.e., revert traffic to baseline immediately; canary version stays configured but receives 0%).

I’ll update the go/no-go doc with scope notes and send you the latest text in a bit.

-Marissa



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 18, 2025 at 11:17 AM PT
Subject: Re: GA go/no-go prep: Hosted canary rollouts (Console workflow)

Adding Security view.

I’m not seeing a GA blocker, but I want to be precise about what we’re promising:

1) Audit event coverage
- Required for GA: create, update (incl. step schedule edits), start, pause, resume, rollback, approve/deny, and any system-initiated action (auto-stop/auto-rollback) with an explicit reason code.
- Please confirm we emit “preview/validate” as non-audit telemetry only (fine), and that the audit event payload includes:
  - actor identity (user id + email), actor type (human/service), tenant id
  - route id, baseline version id, canary version id
  - before/after diff (at least for % split and state transitions)

2) Retention/export messaging
- For GA: we can say “audit events are available in the Console and via export API,” but we should not claim SIEM integrations unless they’re actually supported for Hosted customers.
- Please ensure docs avoid “immutable” language; we can say “tamper-evident” only if we have the cryptographic chain in place (I don’t believe we do for this release).

3) RBAC / approvals
- We need the “rollout approver” role to be present in the RBAC bundle at launch, even if customers don’t use approvals. Otherwise the governance story is shaky.

Action for me: I’ll review the audit event examples in the docs PR once you point me at the latest commit.

Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Product Security
Redwood Inference



From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 18, 2025 at 12:36 PM PT
Subject: Re: GA go/no-go prep: Hosted canary rollouts (Console workflow)

Super helpful — thanks both.

Marissa:
- +1 on adding the beta learnings. The support ticket I’ll reference is the “rollout paused unexpectedly after latency spike” one (SUP-48302). I’ll also mention split mismatch (SUP-48377) as “resolved + covered by tests.”
- Rollback semantics: confirmed with routing folks — rollback immediately sets canary cohort to 0% and routes 100% to baseline; config remains for post-mortem but is locked until resumed or terminated.

Naomi:
- Audit coverage: we have create/start/pause/resume/rollback/approve + system-initiated pause/rollback with reason. We also log step-change (traffic %) and schedule edits.
- Preview/validate: NOT in audit log; it’s request telemetry only.
- Payload fields: actor + tenant + route + baseline/canary version ids are present. For diffs: we currently store structured “changed_fields” + old/new for split % and state. For schedule edits it’s summarized (not a full JSON diff). If you need full before/after for schedule, I can flag as “post-GA improvement” but want your take.
- Retention/export language: ack — we’ll remove “immutable,” and stick to “recorded”/“available.”
- RBAC role: rollout-approver is in the policy bundle PR and should be in the release train. I’ll verify it’s included in the GA checklist.

I’ll update the leadership-ready note with:
- Risk table (impact/likelihood/mitigation/owner)
- Staged enablement + kill switch behavior
- Beta learnings + what changed

If you’re ok with it, I’ll treat “schedule full diff” as not required for GA and document the current behavior.

Dylan



From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 18, 2025 at 1:48 PM PT
Subject: Re: GA go/no-go prep: Hosted canary rollouts (Console workflow)

Works for me.

On diffs: I’m comfortable GA’ing without full schedule before/after as long as:
- The customer-visible timeline is clear about what changed (e.g., “Traffic schedule updated” + new step targets)
- The audit record includes enough detail to answer “who changed the split and when”

Naomi — if you disagree, flag it and we’ll revisit.

Dylan: Please send me the leadership snapshot by EOD so I can drop it into the go/no-go agenda doc.

-Marissa
